faq.q: Why won't my colored QR code scan?
faq.a: Scanners need strong contrast with dark modules on a light background. Inverted (light on dark) or low-contrast color pairs fail on many phones. The tool warns you when the colors are risky.
It adds redundancy so the code still scans when part of it is damaged or covered. Low (L) gives the smallest code; High (H) survives about 30% damage but has more, smaller modules.

faq.q: How small can I print it?
faq.a: A good rule is at least 2 cm (about 0.8 in) wide for a short link, and bigger for long content or when people scan from a distance — roughly one-tenth of the scanning distance.
